concepts.title: Lattices, cones, and fans
concepts.blurb: A fan $\Sigma$ in $N_\mathbb{R} = N \otimes \mathbb{R}$ is a finite collection of strongly convex rational polyhedral cones, closed under taking faces and intersections; this combinatorial datum is the input that builds a toric variety.

concepts.title: Affine toric varieties $U_\sigma$
concepts.blurb: Each cone $\sigma$ produces an affine toric variety $U_\sigma = \Spec(\mathbb{C}[\sigma^\vee \cap M])$ where $M = \Hom(N, \mathbb{Z})$ is the dual lattice; the algebraic torus $T = (\mathbb{C}^\times)^n$ sits inside as the open dense orbit corresponding to the zero cone.

concepts.title: The toric dictionary
concepts.blurb: Cones in $\Sigma$ are in inclusion-reversing bijection with $T$-orbits of $X_\Sigma$; the orbit of $\sigma$ has codimension $\dim \sigma$. Rays are codimension-one toric divisors, and refinements of $\Sigma$ correspond to proper birational toric morphisms.

concepts.title: Worked examples: $\mathbb{P}^n$, $\mathbb{P}^1 \times \mathbb{P}^1$, blowups
concepts.blurb: $\mathbb{P}^n$ is the fan whose maximal cones are spanned by all but one of $e_0, \ldots, e_n$ with $\sum e_i = 0$; $\mathbb{P}^1 \times \mathbb{P}^1$ is its product fan; the Hirzebruch surface $F_n$ tilts one cone; blowing up the origin of $\mathbb{A}^2$ subdivides the first quadrant by adding the ray through $(1,1)$.

concepts.title: Cox ring and toric intersection numbers
concepts.blurb: The total coordinate ring $\mathrm{Cox}(X_\Sigma) = \bigoplus_D H^0(X_\Sigma, \mathcal{O}(D))$ is graded by the class group $\mathrm{Cl}(X_\Sigma)$; toric divisors intersect by combinatorial recipes encoded in $\Sigma$, recovering classical numbers like $H \cdot H = 1$ on $\mathbb{P}^2$.

concepts.title: Reflexive polytopes and Batyrev mirror pairs
concepts.blurb: A lattice polytope $\Delta$ is reflexive iff its polar dual $\Delta^\circ$ is also a lattice polytope; Batyrev's construction takes a generic Calabi-Yau hypersurface in the toric Fano $X_\Delta$ and pairs it with one in $X_{\Delta^\circ}$, the original combinatorial source of mirror symmetry.
